display.title: Episode 20: Life in the Hand of the Tongue, Chapter 2
display.summary_short: The hunter brings the lion's milk but one wrong word lands him in prison, until the tongue proves it is king of the body. Plus Shema with eight Beis Yaakov girls and a pen-pal letter.
display.summary_long: The week after Pesach 5742. Uncle Yossi recalls the Seder nights and Eliyahu HaNavi, and says Pesach should give us emunah all year as we wait for Moshiach. Story time recaps the hunter's dream, in which the limbs laughed at the tongue. The hunter presents the sick king with milk from a 'kalbsaw', and the furious king throws him into prison in chains. Eight girls from a Boro Park Beis Yaakov class recite the Shema and share their own name for Tuesday: 'Uncle Yossi Day'. Uncle Yossi explains the Chofetz Chaim's teaching that each person is allotted a set number of words, while words of Torah, prayer and brachos add years to our life. In prison the hunter dreams again: the frightened limbs beg the tongue for help, and the tongue explains that in the king's land 'kalbsaw' means a dog, not a lion. The hunter explains his mistake, the king recovers and rewards him, and Uncle Yossi quotes Shlomo HaMelech: death and life are in the power of the tongue. The show ends with a ten-year-old girl's letter and drawings, Dial-a-Jewish-Story, and the story records.
display.lesson: Death and life are in the power of the tongue: guard your speech, and use your words for Torah, prayer and brachos, which add years to life.
